newsitem.title: UK: LPC-PACIFICORP/ENERGY FINANCING PUT ON HOLD BY DTI.
newsitem.headline: LPC-PACIFICORP/ENERGY FINANCING PUT ON HOLD BY DTI.

text.p: LONDON, Aug 1 (LPC) - The referral of the planned acquisition of Energy Group Plc by US-based PacifiCorp to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission has derailed, at least temporarily, the groundbreaking 4.7 billion stg financing package put together by lead arranger Goldman Sachs.

The decision by Britain's trade and industry secretary Margaret Beckett to refer the bid means that further progress on the deal cannot now happen until November at the earliest, according to one banker close to the deal. As a result the current financing package will lapse and the arrangers will have to reevaluate the deal if and when regulatory approval is forthcoming.
About 2.85 billion stg of the loan package would have been syndicated in the UK with the remainder being raised in the United States.
Beckett announced this morning that she had 'concerns over whether it will be possible to maintain adequate regulatory control over the merged company.'

The Energy Group said in a statement it was 'surprised and disappointed...particularly as PacifiCorp had indicated their willingness to comply with all assurances required by the UK regulatory authorities.'

Despite stock market expectations that the deal was likely to be referred, the decision still came as something of a shock to the arrangers because the reasons for the referral were not entirely clear, bankers said.
'Its disappointing because just about every bank in the city had contacted us about the deal and a launch would have been imminent,' one of the arrangers said.
Under the previous, Conservative, government, seven of the UK's 12 regional electricity companies were taken over by US firms.
